method: ResShift (E02's network and schedule) trained with clDice (E07) + Laplacian edge + MS-SSIM/L1 mix (E08), no minutiae term, on raw (un-normalised) prints of the v3 data; sampled CCDF-style (E09) with t0, start and projection chosen on v3 val. E12_norm_ccdf_cldice_cv without the MSU normalisation (E12 - E26 isolates it)
_normalization: none in the model: it trains on and repairs raw prints (FixedTrainDataset(normalized=False), probes/ not probes_norm/), tiles padded white 255, output pasted back into the raw damaged print (E02/E09). evaluate.py then normalises the output like every other raw-output model (no --rec-normalized); ccdf_sweep.py scores val repairs the same way (normalise, then match against the normalised gallery)

model._inputs: x_t (1) + cond: raw damaged print, mask, cos 2theta, sin 2theta (4)

training.data: FixedTrainDataset(normalized=False) on v3: 6,308 crops x 6 contaminants x 3 copies = 113,544 samples, severity 0-0.8, raw (not normalised)

aux._note: E07/E08's terms and gate (fpr.training.aux_losses). lam null = set by train.py --calibrate 20 (calibration.json) so each term is ~20% of L_diff at init, as E07 and E08 did; recalibrated here on raw v3 prints (E12 calibrated on normalised v3: clDice 0.38, edge 0.26, mix 0.24; E07/E08 on raw v2: clDice 0.19, edge 0.27, mix 0.12)

ccdf._note: one_call = the model's own x0 estimate at t = T from x_T = y0 (E09's e02_x0); also scored: the full 15-step chain from y0 ('plain'). No regression control (E09 showed it within noise of the chain).
ccdf.selection: on v3 val, each repaired raw print normalised (as evaluate.py does) and matched against the normalised gallery: tau = the score at which 1% of the clean (normalised) val samples' impostor comparisons are accepted; among configurations whose FMR at tau is at most plain's + fmr_margin, the highest acceptance rate of genuine comparisons at tau (score 1's quantity); ties -> higher mean genuine score -> fewer steps
